key_insight: Hardware-tailored control pulses can replace gate sequences for modular VQE circuit elements, dramatically cutting runtime while preserving chemistry functionality.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, more noise-resilient quantum chemistry on near-term devices by reducing the time qubits must remain coherent during VQE execution.
method: Use gradient-ascent pulse engineering to optimize pulses directly for the target hardware.
Implement modular VQE building blocks such as single- and double-qubit excitation circuits with tailored pulses.
Assemble larger chemistry ansätze from these optimized pulse-based elements instead of primitive gates.
evidence_signal: On a silicon spin-qubit processor, the authors report single- and double-qubit excitations executed in under 289 ns and 927 ns, with VQE runtime reductions of up to 15.3× versus gate-based implementations.
watch_item: Optimizing whole VQE ansätze as a single pulse becomes intractable at larger problem sizes, so scalability depends on how well the modular pulse elements compose across circuits and hardware settings.
paper_title: Pulse-optimised circuit elements for scalable and noise-resilient quantum chemistry
